newsitem.title: JAPAN: INSIGHT - JGBs to look to stocks for direction.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - JGBs to look to stocks for direction.

text.p: The key June 10-year Japanese government bond futures contract is expected to have a downward bias on Tuesday, as the market focuses on moves in Tokyo share prices for clues to direction.

Share prices are likely to be firmer on Tuesday and JGBs will probably be sold if the Nikkei 225 average manages to stay above the key 20,000 point level, a trader for a trust bank's securities unit said.
"Share prices were firm toward the close of yesterday's trade and ended above 20,000. It seems that they have firm downside support," the trader said.
Fluctuations in the foreign exchange markets are not likely to have much direct impact on JGBs, traders said.

JGBs were not bought much even when the yen surged versus the dollar on Monday, and are therefore unlikely to be sold even if the yen happens to weaken versus the dollar on Tuesday, said a trader for a major brokerage house.
The market will be watching machinery orders data due at 2 p.m. (0500 GMT), which will include March figures and a forecast for the April-June quarter.
The JGB market is much more sensitive to the announcement of key indicators now than in previous months, one trader said.
"From January to March, the market shrugged off the release of key economic data even when the contents suggested that the economy's recovery was strong," the trader said.
Whereas the market was pessmistic about the outlook for the economy in previous months, it is becoming more optimistic now and is starting to pay more respect to economic indicators, he said.
The Nippon Credit Bank and the Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan are expected to announce the terms for their May five-year bank debentures sometime in the afternoon.
